A '''time-varying covariate''' (also called '''time-dependent covariate''') is a term used in [[statistics]], particularly in [[survival analysis]].<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Austin PC, Latouche A, Fine JP | title = A review of the use of time-varying covariates in the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard competing risk regression model | journal = Statistics in Medicine | volume = 39 | issue = 2 | pages = 103–113 | date = January 2020 | pmid = 31660633 | pmc = 6916372 | doi = 10.1002/sim.8399 }}</ref> It reflects the phenomenon that a [[covariate]] is not necessarily constant through the whole study Time-varying covariates are included to represent time-dependent within-individual variation to predict individual responses.<ref>{{Cite book | vauthors = Little TD |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bCFwAgAAQBAJ |title=The Oxford Handbook of Quantitative Methods, Vol. 2: Statistical Analysis |date=2013-02-01 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-993490-4 |pages=397 |language=en}}</ref> For instance, if one wishes to examine the link between area of residence and cancer, this would be complicated by the fact that study subjects move from one area to another. The area of residency could then be introduced in the [[statistical model]] as a time-varying covariate. In survival analysis, this would be done by splitting each study subject into several observations, one for each area of residence. For example, if a person is born at time 0 in area A, moves to area B at time 5, and is diagnosed with cancer at time 8, two observations would be made. One with a length of 5 (5 − 0) in area A, and one with a length of 3 (8 − 5) in area B.
